articles.title: Deutsche Bank upgrades Norsk Hydro on cheap valuation, earnings upside
articles.summary: Investing.com -- Deutsche Bank upgraded Norwegian aluminium producer Norsk Hydro (OL:NHY) to "buy" from "hold" on Monday, saying heavy cuts to consensus estimates mean much of the downside is already priced into the shares.

articles.title: Is the market too bearish on aluminium?
articles.summary: Investing.com -- Investor sentiment toward aluminium has turned excessively bearish despite resilient demand and historically low inventories, according to analysts who expect prices to rise to $3,625 per tonne in 2027.

articles.title: J.P. Morgan puts Norsk Hydro on Negative CW on rising LNG cost risks
articles.summary: Investing.com -- J.P. Morgan placed aluminium producer Norsk Hydro on "Negative Catalyst Watch" ahead of its Nov. 25 capital markets day, saying 2027 EBITDA could be NOK28.28 billion, -15% versus Bloomberg consensus, if the company cannot secure a long-term gas contract for its Alunorte refinery in Brazil and keeps buying spot liquefied natural gas.

articles.title: Goldman cuts Norsk Hydro as falling premiums, rising costs weigh
articles.summary: Investing.com -- Goldman Sachs cut Norwegian aluminium producer Norsk Hydro to "neutral" from "buy" and lowered its price target to NOK 79 from NOK 100, saying falling aluminium premiums and rising costs make 2027 earnings harder to lift.

articles.summary: Norsk Hydro came into this Q3 2026 print with a bruised chart and a flattering reputation. articles.title: Hydro Q3 adjusted core earnings rise 52% but miss forecasts on weak cash flow
articles.summary: Investing.com -- Norwegian aluminium and renewable energy group Hydro on Friday reported a 52% jump in third-quarter adjusted core earnings to 9.09 billion crowns , but the result fell short of analysts’ expectations as weak cash generation and a slump in power earnings offset higher metal prices.

articles.title: BofA Securities names top mining stocks as copper outlook brightens
articles.summary: Investing.com -- BofA Securities has updated its mining sector rankings, elevating several major producers as the investment bank raised its long-term copper price forecast by 20% to $12,000 per ton for 2026. The upgrade reflects persistent supply issues that continue to push copper prices higher, even as analysts monitor risks from potential energy shocks and data center capital expenditure pauses.
